title: Negative possession review
focus: Mix the forms and sentence patterns already taught in this pack.
targetSkills: Regular singular partitive in negative possession

exercises.prompt: Choose “You do not have a ball.” in Finnish. Use sinulla (“you as the owner”) and palloa (“a ball”). Frame: “Sinulla ___ palloa”. Address one person.
exercises.explanation: Use fixed ei ole with every possessor. The owner does not change the negative verb to en, emme, or eivät.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Fixed ei ole in possession: form or meaning confused

Use fixed ei ole with every possessor. The owner does not change the negative verb to en, emme, or eivät.
Use fixed ei ole with every possessor. The owner does not change the negative verb to en, emme, or eivät. This choice uses the wrong verb form.
This choice changes the required polarity or leaves the required question pattern.

sentenceExplanation.translation: You do not have a ball.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed ei ole + singular partitive noun

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: sinä has the learned possession form sinulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Possession uses fixed ei with every owner; do not change it to en, emme, or eivät.
After ei, olla uses ole. Together ei ole means “do not have” or “does not have” here.
pallo + -a = palloa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed ei ole in possession: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.

exercises.prompt: Choose the noun in “You do not have a ball.” Frame: “Sinulla ei ole ___.” Use pallo (“a ball”). Address one person.
exercises.explanation: Negative possession uses the singular partitive noun. For this regular word, pallo + -a = palloa; keep both vowels when they meet.
requiredSkills: Regular singular partitive in negative possession
exercises.targetSkill: Regular singular partitive in negative possession
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Regular singular partitive in negative possession: form or meaning confused

optionFeedback.pallo: The basic noun form does not express the required negative possession here.
optionFeedback.palloä: Choose -a with back vowels a, o, u; choose -ä with front vowels ä, ö, y or only neutral e, i.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: The negative frame ei ole needs the partitive noun: add the ending taught for this regular word.
